tools.name: codex_doctor
tools.description: Check whether the local Codex CLI is installed, recent enough, signed in and able to load its configuration, and report the exact steps to fix it if not. Run this when any other tool reports the CLI is unavailable, or before relying on delegation for the first time. It only inspects the installation; it never installs or changes anything.

refresh.description: Re-probe the CLI instead of reusing the cached diagnosis.

working_dir.description: Absolute directory to run the check in. Codex loads the configuration of the directory it runs in, so pass the one a delegation would use. Defaults to this server's own.

tools.name: list_codex_models
tools.description: List the Codex models available on this machine, with the reasoning-effort levels each one supports. Read from the installed Codex CLI, with a warned static fallback if its catalog cannot be read. Call this before codex_delegate when choosing a model explicitly.

refresh.description: Bypass the cache and re-read the catalog from the CLI.

working_dir.description: Absolute directory to read the catalog in. A project you have trusted in Codex can set its own catalog, so pass the directory a delegation would use. Defaults to this server's own.

tools.name: codex_recommend
tools.description: Given a task description, recommend which Codex model and reasoning effort to delegate it with. Runs no model call; applies a documented matrix reconciled against the installed catalog.

task_description.description: What the delegated task involves, in one or two sentences.

priority.description: Bias the reasoning effort: quality raises it, latency and cost lower it. Default balanced.

working_dir.description: Absolute directory whose Codex configuration and model catalog should be used. Defaults to this server's own.

tools.name: codex_delegate
tools.description: Delegate a task to the local Codex CLI (OpenAI's coding agent), choosing model and reasoning effort. Use it when the user asks for Codex, or when handing work off clearly serves their request: a second opinion from a different model family, or an investigation that would otherwise flood this conversation. When the user has not named a model, call codex_recommend first and present its suggested model and effort to the user in the same message in which you say you are going to delegate, then pass both explicitly here. That recommendation is advice for an already-authorised delegation, not a replacement for the user's own preference. Everything passed in prompt, context and target_files is sent to OpenAI, and every run spends the user's own Codex usage, so do not delegate what you can answer directly, and tell the user when you delegate. Codex runs read-only unless a different default sandbox is configured. Set sandbox to workspace-write to let it edit files. Codex cannot see this conversation, so pass everything it needs in prompt, context, and target_files.

prompt.description: The task for Codex. Be specific and self-contained: Codex cannot see this conversation.

model.description: Catalog slug from list_codex_models. If omitted, the configured default is used; with no default configured the call is refused and the recommended model is returned.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning depth, independent of model choice. Uses the configured default or the model's default when omitted. Clamped to supported levels within the configured ceiling; refused if none qualify.

system_instructions.description: Persona or extra rules inherited from the orchestrator, layered on the built-in quality contract.

context.description: Background Codex needs: prior findings, constraints, relevant excerpts.

target_files.description: Paths Codex should focus on, relative to working_dir.

acceptance_criteria.description: Concrete conditions that must hold for the task to be considered done.

working_dir.description: Absolute path Codex uses as its working root.

sandbox.description: Sandbox policy. Uses the configured default when omitted; without one, Codex runs read-only.

auto_approve.description: Adds --approve-for-me so Codex auto-approves its own commands. Only applies when sandbox is workspace-write.

add_dirs.description: Additional absolute directories that should be writable alongside working_dir.

use_worktree.description: Run in a managed git worktree. Writes outside it remain subject to the sandbox policy and add_dirs.

web_search.description: Enable Codex's API-backed live web-search tool for this run. In a read-only sandbox, shell commands have no network access, so this is the route to current external information. When omitted, Codex's own configured web_search mode applies.

skip_git_repo_check.description: Allow running outside a git repository.

mode.description: blocking (default) waits and streams progress; background returns a job_id immediately.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema object for this turn's final message, which then comes back as JSON in a delimited block. OpenAI's structured outputs apply: every object needs "additionalProperties": false and every property listed in "required". At most 64 KiB serialised.

tools.name: codex_follow_up
tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a previous delegation using its thread_id. Codex retains the earlier context, so only the new instruction needs to be sent. Like a delegation, it is sent to OpenAI and spends the user's Codex usage.

thread_id.description: The thread_id reported by a previous codex_delegate call.

model.description: Override the model for this turn. Defaults to the thread's last model from memory or, on a registry miss, Codex's session file; if neither has it, the configured default, else the call is refused.

reasoning_effort.description: Override the reasoning effort for this turn. Defaults to the thread's last effort when the model is unchanged, otherwise to the configured or model default.

sandbox.description: Sandbox policy for this turn. Uses the configured default when omitted; read-only when unset.

auto_approve.description: Not supported on follow-ups: true is refused and nothing runs.

working_dir.description: Absolute directory to resume in. Defaults to the directory the thread last ran in.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema object for this turn's final message, which then comes back as JSON in a delimited block. OpenAI's structured outputs apply: every object needs "additionalProperties": false and every property listed in "required". At most 64 KiB serialised.

tools.name: codex_job_status
tools.description: Report the state and recent activity of a background delegation started with mode=background. Call it with no job_id to list every known job.

include_activity.description: Include the recent progress log for the job.

tools.name: codex_job_result
tools.description: Return the full output of a finished background delegation. Errors if the job is still running.
